verdicts.reason: A stacks in a sensible top-down order with both badges grouped, but the headline and body run almost to the left edge with a tiny margin, the can is shrunk and small, and the legal text is crammed against the bottom edge. B uses a cleaner two-column split, but it breaks the badge pair apart: FREE DELIVERY is a stretched pill sitting on the circle at the top, and 4 FLAVOURS is stranded alone in the bottom-left corner, so the grouping is lost.

In A the Order Now button nearly collides with the legal text directly under it. The headline sits below the product, the badges are jammed into the top-left corner over the circle, and the side margins are very thin. B has a readable two-column layout with a strong headline and CTA, but the badges are split up (a stretched FREE DELIVERY on top, an orphaned 4 FLAVOURS bottom-left) and the legal text is tiny.

A is a real re-layout: the headline and CTA are clear and the can is a good size. Its flaws are the scattered, stretched badge pills and very small legal text. B is just the original banner shrunk into a letterbox strip in the middle of the square, with huge empty bands above and below. The badge and legal text can't be read, and the Order Now button is cut off at the right edge.

A is the shrunk letterbox copy of the banner: microscopic badge and legal text, mostly empty canvas, and a CTA clipped at the right edge, so it is unusable. B is a proper top-down re-layout with a dominant headline and CTA, but the left margin is cramped, the can is small, and the badges are wedged into the top-left corner over the circle.
